CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region is Pringsewu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pringsewu. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Pringsewu Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus in Pringsewu Regency. 7. Woman is an adult human of female gender. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or misery whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women is any act of violence against women that results in or may result in suffering or misery to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering or misery to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 17. Neglect is the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope for which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children is all activities... to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 26. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant is a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling therapy advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

Article 2

The implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of rights and equal human dignity, non-discrimination, equality and gender justice as well as protection of human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services covering aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

CHAPTER XI

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 5

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the region.

Article 12

Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is disUiph to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 21

( 1) PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and reporting mechanisms as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 26

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Pringsewu Regency.

Enacted in Pringsewu on date S MC\~ 10 \S

REGENT OF PRINGSEWU,

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions operating in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12

Letter a

Sufficiently clear.

Letter b

What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain statements, declarations, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter c

Sufficiently clear.

Letter d

What is meant by "the right to continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" includes: the right to have their rights advocated and access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of reputation, and citizenship.

Letter e

What is meant by "the right to confidential handling" is the right of victims to have their identity kept confidential at all stages of handling by officers.

Letter f

What is meant by "the right to psychological and legal assistance" is a right that includes assistance by: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members.

Letter g

Sufficiently clear.

Article 25

(1) Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to action and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations;

I

(2) PPT managers who in carrying out tasks of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementation of protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

Article 24

(1) The regional government is obliged to allocate budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in implementing the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Budget allocation as referred to in paragraph ( 1) is adjusted to the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 17

Paragraph (1)

Letter a

Sufficiently clear.

Letter b

Sufficiently clear.

Letter c

What is meant by medicolegal is the effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.

Letter d

Sufficiently clear.

Letter e

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (3)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (4)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (5)

What is meant by "safe house" is a temporary shelter intended to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. Temporary protection is provided for a period of up to 14 (fourteen) days and can be extended according to the victim's condition. PPT that do not have a shelter can network with PPT that have a shelter.

b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or

(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

( 4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purpose of evidence in the field of law.

(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.

(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

Child victim of violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or misery whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women is any act of violence against women that results in or may result in suffering or misery to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering or misery to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 17. Neglect is the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope for which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children is all activities... to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 26. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services covering aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

CHAPTER XI

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all I prostitution or indecent acts.

Article 19

(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions operating in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

1. Region is Pringsewu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pringsewu. 4. Woman is an adult human of female gender. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or misery whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women is any act of violence against women that results in or may result in suffering or misery to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering or misery to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 17. Neglect is the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope for which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 5

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the region.

Article 2

The implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect and recognition of rights and equal human dignity, non-discrimination, equality and gender justice as well as protection of human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

Article 21

( 1) PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and reporting mechanisms as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services covering aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

CHAPTER XI

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER VIII

PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 12

Letter a

Sufficiently clear.

Letter b

What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain statements, declarations, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter c

Sufficiently clear.

Letter d

What is meant by "the right to continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" includes: the right to have their rights advocated and access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of reputation, and citizenship.

Letter e

What is meant by "the right to confidential handling" is the right of victims to have their identity kept confidential at all stages of handling by officers.

Letter f

What is meant by "the right to psychological and legal assistance" is a right that includes assistance by: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members.

Letter g

Sufficiently clear.

Article 24

(1) The regional government is obliged to allocate budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in implementing the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Budget allocation as referred to in paragraph ( 1) is adjusted to the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 12

Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is disUiph to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 19

(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of PPT.

(2) PPT in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection in its implementation may establish partnerships with Social Community Institutions operating in the field of protection of Women and Children.

(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

activities, defense and security as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.

What is meant by "protection of human rights of women and children" is providing basic rights in the form of a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on a court order.

What is meant by "best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies must be a primary consideration.

CHAPTER IV

FORMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 25

(1) Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to action and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations;

I

(2) PPT managers who in carrying out tasks of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementation of protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and reporting mechanisms as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) which are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 21

( 1) PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and reporting mechanisms as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 24

(1) The regional government is obliged to allocate budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in implementing the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Budget allocation as referred to in paragraph ( 1) is adjusted to the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION Article 22

(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.

(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 25

(1) Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to action and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations;

I

(2) PPT managers who in carrying out tasks of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of implementation of protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with PPT internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

Article 12

Letter a

Sufficiently clear.

Letter b

What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain statements, declarations, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter c

Sufficiently clear.

Letter d

What is meant by "the right to continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" includes: the right to have their rights advocated and access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of reputation, and citizenship.

Letter e

What is meant by "the right to confidential handling" is the right of victims to have their identity kept confidential at all stages of handling by officers.

Letter f

What is meant by "the right to psychological and legal assistance" is a right that includes assistance by: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members.

Letter g

Sufficiently clear.

Article 12

Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: every unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is disUiph to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Woman is an adult human of female gender. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or misery whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women is any act of violence against women that results in or may result in suffering or misery to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering or misery to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 17. Neglect is the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope for which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children is all activities... to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 26. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant is a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling therapy advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 21

( 1) PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and reporting mechanisms as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PRINGSEWU REGENCY NUMBER YEAR 2015

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services covering aspects of prevention, service and assistance, reunification and empowerment.

Article 5

The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes prevention, service and empowerment efforts for victims of violence in the region.

Article 24

(1) The regional government is obliged to allocate budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in implementing the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Budget allocation as referred to in paragraph ( 1) is adjusted to the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 11

Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e is caused by: '

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and / or

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all I prostitution or indecent acts.

Article 20

(1) Forms of protection provided to Victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of protection:

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of the victim carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

( 4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for the purpose of evidence in the field of law.

(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in solving problems.

(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Child victim of violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or misery whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women is any act of violence against women that results in or may result in suffering or misery to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering or misery to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 17. Neglect is the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope for which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children is all activities... to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 26. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant is a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling therapy advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.

Article 26

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.
