IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens. The amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness of the importance of protecting human rights and the constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so their dignity and dignity need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and nature without discrimination.

Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, so they need to get protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

The regional government together with the community is obliged to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER V

RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 21

( 1) PPT reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) The Head of SKPD in charge of women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Regent.

(3) The Regent reports the protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and reporting mechanisms as referred to in paragraphs (1) through (3) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region is Pringsewu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pringsewu. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Pringsewu Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the regional apparatus in Pringsewu Regency. 7. Woman is an adult human of female gender. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or misery either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or misery whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women is any act of violence against women that results in or may result in suffering or misery to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 13. Violence against children is any action that results in suffering or misery to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 17. Neglect is the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope for which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting to work properly inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women has occurred or will occur. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children is all activities... to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others. 26. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Assistant is a person or institution that has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling therapy advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face. 32.
